spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The disorder that burst forth from governing falsities and evils as a gross external principle rose up against the revealed pattern of Divine mediation. It was severed from that higher place and cast down into the lowest degree, because ordered interior states would not admit it into their harmonies. When it entered the lowest level of life it organized itself into a fixed system of perverted perception, established itself in that system, and produced works from it; and when those malformed works again collapsed into the lowest level, the same disorder returned within them and re‑entered the governing falsities.

Within those works it took on their quality and spoke through the chief ruling falsity. That leading falsity urged its allied falsities to contribute their borrowed insight so that a human likeness could be fabricated, modeled on the loftier pattern. They yielded what they had, and from it the imitation of true humanity was produced.

That same gross external influence—which had already perceived the Divine pattern, organized a perverted system, and lodged within it—afterward rose again within the resulting works and passed into the governing powers. By its driving force they produced an inner and outer human appearance after the loftier pattern. Through the efficacy of this disorder, entering by means of those works, it took possession of the rulers; and under its impulse they generated successive states from themselves, each according to its ruling inclination, some retaining a likeness to the true form and others losing it.

So understand this: the lower governing powers shaped the first human state through the activity of disorder entering them by means of works, and thus established a human form according to the loftier pattern.

Then the formative power arranged within that human form capacities for receiving and acting, outwardly and inwardly, distributed into ordered regions. For whatever these capacities and their elemental operations take in from the outermost life, there are inward retentive powers and ordered recesses, so that what is received can be preserved. When inquiry is made for what has been deposited within, each capacity draws out what it received and supplies it to the one who seeks it.

Thus the outward capacity for discernment is furnished with power to notice every kind of presented quality and to keep each kind within its inward retention.

Likewise, that same outward discernment has inward retentive powers capable of receiving every appearance it takes in—whether aligned with good or with evil, whether it stirs love, aversion, or craving. When it chooses, it can enter its inner retentions, search and recollect what was stored, and bring it forward for the inquirer—whether it serves craving, genuine love, or aversion; and so it acts according to the kind of reception.

The capacity that receives instruction also holds what it takes in—whether good or evil—within inner memory, preserving it through long duration. Even after long duration, when inquiry is made for what it once received, it immediately searches its inner records, finds that particular teaching, and produces it from the state in which it was first preserved.

In the same way, the capacity that discerns subtle quality takes in what it perceives and deposits it in inward memory; when questioned it returns to those memories and recalls only what it retained.

Further, the capacity that discerns appropriations and delights gathers such perceptions into its own inward retentions; whenever inquiry is made about a particular delight, it can recall it and supply even its distinctive sign, giving the remembered quality to the one who asks.

Again, the capacity of direct contact with the outermost receives the memory of that contact and stores it inwardly until inquiry is made; then it returns, draws out what it retained, and gives it to whoever asks.

Over all these is the central governing love-and-thought which presides as the chief faculty: whatever the five outward capacities receive and entrust to it, it receives and guards; and whenever their deposit is requested, it brings forth and returns all that was given to it.

For the deliberation of this central faculty is like a ruling authority: with it are subordinate reasonings and directive powers for action; when these ask for what they desire, it supplies the judgment and counsel by which they proceed.

And it is also like an inward steward: whatever is entrusted to it, it receives and arranges distinctly in ordered forms and distinct states, and it can produce each again from the very state in which it was placed.

So too the coordinating power for outward action can bring forth again, from inward retention, whatever discernment has stored and whatever is requested.

Likewise it can bring forth again whatever receptivity to instruction has stored, whenever that remembered teaching is called for.

The remaining outward capacities follow the same order: what each has stored can be produced and supplied whenever it is requested.

Yet protections stand at these entrances, and restraints are fixed there under the authority of those protections.

It is like a guarded system of admission: restraints are set upon the approaches; vigilant powers govern those restraints at the point of entry. What is native to the ruling love and agrees with it is admitted; what is foreign to it is resisted and held outside; and something else may be admitted only with difficulty. Within are many inner containments and many controlling restraints; and when the directing power chooses, it handles the restraints, opens admission, and draws out what had been hidden.

So the whole outward life is like a powerful organized domain, and its admissions and their guards are the outermost access points of the human life—by which discernment, instruction, and subtle discrimination take in influences, and by which formed thoughts are expressed. Many sentinels are set over the outer faculties to protect their admissions; and the directive faculty within can open or shut them as it wills.

But when enlightened understanding from Divine truth approaches to enter these outer admissions, the governing falsities and evils that serve as gatekeepers resist and restrain it, binding the whole outer circuit so that what they treat as alien cannot enter.

Nevertheless, enlightened understanding by wisdom, reverence, and persistent effort subdues those guards and takes control of the restraints upon every admission. Then the admissions that were formerly opened to craving—admitting delighting appearances, transmitting speech devoted to worldly entanglements, and admitting appropriations that mingle what is unclean with disorder—are no longer used for such reception; and when one ceases to admit these, the inner ruling love and thought follow after.

Thus, because the restraints upon the life of the regenerating person are held by enlightened understanding within, that person is opened to admit what accords with the Divine. Discernment is opened to receive perceptions of genuine love, justice, and righteousness. What formerly appeared attractive—splendid persuasive appearances crafted to adorn craving and excite self-love—no longer delights, because craving that once ruled has been humbled by the indwelling enlightened understanding. The displays of craving become repugnant, while the qualities of the Divine—justice, humility, and the preference for simple truths not fashioned for self-display—are pleasing.

Likewise the capacity for instruction, once open to vain teachings, seductive persuasions, and concealed practices of evil, now finds such things repugnant and refuses them. Instead it delights to receive teachings of justice, worshipful affections, elevations of prayer, acknowledgement of the Divine, instruction of truth, and understanding of charity.

In sum, the outer admissions that were once open to evil are now opened to good. Disorder once ruled the outward life without higher command; but now its authority in the outward faculties is taken away. Living good from the Divine becomes lord over all operations, binding them in stable harmony and confirming them in the certainty of truth. The outer admissions are opened to good; good enters by discernment and instruction and dwells in the central governing love. Divine influence reigns, annulling disorder as the initiating impulse and final purpose, and establishing instead the Divine willing and the intention of enlightened understanding.

Therefore, by wisdom and practiced skill, set firm protection around the outer circuit of life’s admissions, so that the disorder that still presses upon the outer level has no power to steal your understanding of truth, scatter it into conflicting states, or drive it through shifting distortions.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coheres strongly as a single instruction on how disorder descends into the outermost life, fabricates an imitation of humanity, and then how regeneration operates through guarded admissions and ordered inner retentions. The middle section shifts into a systematic description of receptive capacities and memory; it remains coherent as an anatomy of spiritual cognition. Minor stumbles come from textual lacunae (¶2 ending, ¶16 fragment) and repeated lines, but the spiritual narrative remains continuous and consistent in voice.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from physical damage: the narrative is coherent in correspondential terms (Matter as an invasive impulse moving through levels and re-entering via fruits/abortions), but the end of the paragraph is lacunose, creating an abrupt jump in agency and sequence.
findings.evidence: Text: "And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [it came up again in them and entered the rulers]". The spiritual reading explicitly flags this: "End of paragraph is textually broken" and supplies a smoothing paraphrase. Removing anything won’t improve coherence; the break is caused by missing text, not a secondary overlay.

findings.diagnosis: Clean substrate transition: mythic cosmogony (sin/Matter, rulers, Adam/Eve) is being used functionally as an etiology for how a counterfeit ‘image’ is fabricated by an invading power. No administrative inventory, no jurisdictional rank-listing; the rulers act as a single functional complex.
findings.evidence: Text is driven by what the entities DO: "Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image" (¶3); "Through the energy of the sin... it went into the (rulers) through the fruits" (¶4). The reading notes it can reduce "ruler/companions" to functions without strain, and reports no stumble beyond ordinary mythic language.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential teaching: the chapter shifts from cosmogonic etiology to a functional ‘inner anatomy’ of reception, storage, and recall. The voice is consistently functional (storehouses/repositories/cavities; receiving, depositing, bringing out).
findings.evidence: Text repeatedly teaches by function: "internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored" (¶6); each sense-faculty "receive[s]... and place[s]" (¶8-¶12); the heart "receive[s] and guard[s]" deposits from the five (¶13). The spiritual reading reports this section "coheres strongly" and does not need to force alien categories; its only accommodation is interpretive (e.g., smell/taste as discrimination/appropriation), not a narrative repair.

findings.diagnosis: Metaphorical elaboration that remains within the same functional pedagogical mode. Although ‘king / advisers / leaders of the army’ can look like governance language, here it serves as an analogy for internal deliberation coordinating subordinate functions, not a jurisdictional list of cosmic officers.
findings.evidence: Text: "For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the advisers of his city and the leaders of his army are placed with him" (¶14); and "it is like a cellarman... put in separate vessels" (¶15). The spiritual reading does not stumble; it interprets these as "subordinate reasonings and directive powers" and as an internal stewarding function. Crucially, there are no proper names, no stations, no numbered ranks—so the ‘administrative’ imagery functions as a simile inside a correspondential lesson.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from fragmentary transmission: this is the tail of ¶15’s simile, but the manuscript is broken and the clause is incomplete, forcing the reader to supply the missing object and verb.
findings.evidence: Text: "... in the place that it put it." The spiritual reading notes: "Source is fragmentary; rendered as completion of the prior sentence." This is a classic torn-line continuation rather than an insertion.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation with minor scribal-style redundancy: the ‘faculty of the body’ reprises the earlier storage/retrieval mechanism at a higher integrative level. ¶18 repeats a full clause, which reads like dittography/emphatic repetition rather than a voice change.
findings.evidence: Text: ¶18 has near-duplication: "It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked." The spiritual reading flags it as "Repetition in source preserved as emphasis." Nothing about the repetition introduces administrative rank or new actors; it stays in the same functional schema.

findings.diagnosis: Clean extension of the same correspondential model using ‘watchmen/bolts/camp’ imagery. Despite ‘guards/sentinels’ language, it is not an administrative overlay: the imagery concretely maps to orifices, access-control, and permissions (open/shut) as functions of cognition and habit.
findings.evidence: Text explicitly interprets its own metaphor: "This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates... are like the orifices and organs of the body" (¶22). The spiritual reading does not stumble and treats citizen/foreigner as congruent/incongruent inputs. There are still no named archons, stations, watches by number, etc.—so the ‘guard’ language is pedagogical analogy, not Mani’s jurisdictional administration.

findings.diagnosis: Clean moral-ascetical climax continuous with the gate/orifice metaphor. The ‘Light Mind’ confrontation with ‘rulers/guards’ remains functional (who holds the bolts; what enters; what is sealed/bound), not administrative taxonomy. No seam markers or fivefold systematizing addendum appear; the exhortation in ¶29 is an organic conclusion.
findings.evidence: Text: "Light Mind... humble the guards... take... bolts" (¶24); "authority has been taken from the Sin... sealed... chain of peace" (¶28); ends with direct practical admonition (¶29). The spiritual reading reports strong coherence and identifies no forced repairs here—only straightforward development from ‘memory storehouses’ to ‘guarded orifices’ to ‘regeneration’.

textual_criticism.summary: 8 findings: 2 genuine difficulties due to damaged text (¶2, ¶16); 1 mixed-but-functional simile cluster (¶14-¶15) judged coherent; 5 clean correspondential sections confirmed (¶3-¶5, ¶6-¶13, ¶17-¶19, ¶20-¶22, ¶23-¶29). No administrative overlay blocks and no insertions requiring excision were detected; the spiritual reading’s only stumbles align with lacunae and minor redundancy, not secondary administrative layering.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [it came up again in them and entered the rulers]

[And when it came up] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [the form of Adam and Eve after the likeness of the exalted one].

The sin that s[purted out from the rulers,] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [fruits and assumed them]. It went in to the rulers [and by its power] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[ted with it. And they] begat each of them according to his destiny [in their generations]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.
Behold, I have taught you this lesson, how the rulers shaped Adam and Eve by the action of the sin that went into the [m] through the fruits, and he was ordained after the image of the exalted one.

The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.
In this way his faculty [of the eyes has] outer [limbs] to look at [all sights,] every type with [in its storehouses.]

Also [the fa]culty of the eyes [has] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the] time and think and seek [every image that it stored within,] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t]ed it—whether it be something from lu[stful thing,]n image of love [or something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.

The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [inner storehouses] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.

[In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [to its inner repositories] and [seek in its] storehouse and remember [these odours] only these things.

However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [it wishes,] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.

Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.

And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.

For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.

Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [if they ask it for what was entrusted to it, it brings it out]
... in the place that it put it.

This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.

Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.

Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds too,] they shall bring it out in to [its storehouses and repositories] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!

Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [behind them,] that [and locks and bolts;] there are a mass [within] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [of the gates] are [many,] Whenever someone will wish [to bring out,] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.

This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.

However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.

Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.

So, now, bec[ause] the b[olt]s to the body of the righteous person are in the hands of the Light M[in]d within, he is open [to receive] in all that is pleasing to God. He is op[en to take] in by his eyes the visions of lov[e and justice] and righteousness. Indeed, due to this, the si[ghts and] the [ad]ornme[nt of the gar]ments of kings, which are woven with gold; and the garments of silken wom[en], which are woven with gold and pearls, made beautiful for the shape of lust; first they were lovable before the eyes of the chosen person. Yet, now, by the power of the Light Mind that has suffused him and lived in the body he has humbled lust, the goddess of the body. The parades of lust have become loathsome in the presence of the righteous person. How-ever, the aspects of divinity and righteousness and humility and scorned clothes are pleasing to him.

Again, [these] ears were first opening to empty sounds and to the melodies of lust, to the secrecies of [wic]kedness. All these were pleasing at first, at the time when he he[a]rd them. Yet, now, by the power of the Light Mind, the sounds of lust and the words of magic and evil mysteries have become loathsome in his presence; as he is not pleased to hear them from this time on. Rather, he likes all the time to listen to the sounds of the lessons of righteousness, the words of the psalms and of the prayers, the praise of the hymns and the lessons of truth, and the knowledge of charity.

[S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.

Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [S]in, the begin-ning and the end. [In contrast], the will of the [Holy Spirit] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.

With wisdom and skill make yourselves secure at the circuit of the body's orifices, so that the sin that dwells in the body has no power over you. Nor does it take from you your light, nor scatter it from place to place, nor (drive) it from site to site in various forms.
